releaseNotes:
Welcome to Market Mania 6.0
This is the biggest update yet. Your shop now grows over 50 store levels, with new products, freezers, deliveries by truck, UPI payments, mess to clean, and much more.
Use Next and Previous to read each page. Finish on the last page takes you back to the game.
Your saved game carries on exactly where you left it: your level, your stock and everything you could sell are kept.

50 store levels
The store now has 50 levels, and each one comes a little faster than before.
Every item a customer buys earns 1 XP. An item a customer cannot find, or finds too expensive, costs 1 XP. A level once reached is never lost.
Every level brings a few more customers through the door.
The Shop Floor shows your level and how far through it you are, for example Level 5, 40%. The old store rating has gone.
Something new opens at almost every level up to 50, with a few quiet levels in between. MarketHub, BuildMax and HireNow say which level each thing needs.
Two new achievements: reach store level 30, and reach the top level, 50.

Licences and new products
A new shop starts with six everyday basics: Rice, Flour, Lentils, Sugar, Salt and Sunflower Oil.
Everything else comes in small licence packs of two to five products, from the Snacks licence at level 2 to the Pet Food licence at level 46. Licenses on the Computer lists what is in every pack.
29 new products: Instant Noodles, Pasta, Cornflakes, Honey, Jam, Peanut Butter, Sliced Bread, Cake, Bottled Water, Toffees, Eggs, Cheese Slices, Tomato Ketchup, Mayonnaise, Chilli Sauce, Hand Wash, Toilet Paper, Toilet Cleaner, Carrots, Garlic, Mangoes, Lemons, Frozen Peas, French Fries, Ice Cream, Frozen Pizza, Frozen Chicken, Dog Food and Cat Food.
Four new categories in MarketHub: Bakery, Sauces, Frozen and Pet Food. Every product comes in a Low price, a Medium price and a Premium brand.

Freezers, fridges and produce stands
Frozen food needs a freezer. Buy a Small or Large Freezer from MarketHub. Frozen food only goes in a freezer, and a freezer only holds frozen food.
Dairy still lives in fridges. The Small Fridge now opens at level 3, with the Breakfast licence.
Fresh fruit and vegetables are sold from produce stands, by the kilogram, and weighed at the checkout.
Fridges and freezers add more to the electricity bill than racks do.

Deliveries and the Loading Dock
Orders now come by truck. Choose the size, Small for 10 boxes, Medium for 20 or Large for 40, and the speed: Express in 30 minutes, Standard in 60 or Economy in 120. Faster costs more.
The Loading Dock page shows each truck. Open the warehouse door and the truck door, then carry the boxes in, or ask your stock clerks to unload.
Deliver Inside has the driver carry everything into the warehouse for a small fee.
Rain can make a truck late, and now and then a box arrives damaged: send it back for a refund, or keep what is left of it.
Buy your own trucks for free delivery, paying only for fuel, and up to three loading docks to unload several trucks at once.
Big orders get a bulk discount: 3 percent from 20 boxes, 5 percent from 40.

MarketHub
Wholesale prices change every day, product by product, by up to 10 percent.
Three products are on a deal each day, 15 to 30 percent off. A shortage can make a product dearer for one to three days. Each product says so in MarketHub.
Deliveries in MarketHub shows every truck on its way.
Repeat Last Order fills the cart with your last order in one press.
Auto-Order, from level 19, orders a product by itself whenever it runs low.

Warehouse, trolley and pallet jack
The warehouse groups its boxes by product, so a long list is quick to get through.
The Hand Trolley carries four boxes at once, to the racks or from a truck. Stock the racks straight from the trolley.
The Pallet Jack moves a whole pallet off a truck in one go.
Warehouse Expansions open at levels 3, 7, 18 and 31, and the warehouse can grow to 150 boxes.

Your staff
Stock clerks unload trucks, use the trolley and the pallet jack, and restock several racks in one round.
Stock clerks now open sealed boxes themselves when no opened box is left, so they keep the shelves full without your help.
Choose each clerk's duty on the Warehouse page: unloading, restocking or both.
Cashiers finish the customer at their desk before they go on a break.
Hire security guards to stop shoplifters at the door.
Every worker opens at their own store level in HireNow.

Checkout and payments
Customers can now pay by UPI. Press Show QR Code, and the screen tells you as the customer scans it, pays on their phone, and the payment is received. If their phone loses its connection, show the code again.
About four customers in ten pay by UPI, a third by card, and the rest in cash. Card and UPI money goes straight to the bank.
The card keypad speaks the amount as you type each digit, says which digit Delete took off, and says Cleared.
Self-checkout machines serve card and UPI customers with up to 8 items. Now and then one needs your help.
A customer now waits 1 minute 40 seconds at the checkout before giving up.
Checkout is on the Shop Floor from the very start of a new game.
The End of Day report counts UPI payments too.

Shoplifters
At the exit gate you can check the receipt, let the shoplifter go, or hit them. Hitting gets the stock back but costs the store 1 XP.
A security guard on shift stops most shoplifters at the door. You hear the hit and the shoplifter's cry.
Security Cameras make half as many people try to shoplift.
Stop a thief in the warehouse and you hear them cry out too.

Mess and cleaning
Customers now make a mess: spills, broken glass, litter, and muddy footprints on rainy days. Up to three at a time.
You find a mess when you reach its rack. Put a Wet Floor Sign by a spill or broken glass, then mop or sweep it up. Cleaning takes 2 to 5 game minutes, and the button says how long.
Cleaners clean every mess by themselves, oldest first, with a sign out while they work.
A spill or broken glass with no sign upsets every customer in the aisles. A mess left more than 15 minutes costs the store XP.
Cleaning on the Computer lists every mess and who is cleaning it.

Grow your shop
Store Expansions let more customers in at once: up to 25, opening at levels 16, 28, 40 and 50.
Buy more baskets in BuildMax, within what your store can hold.
Rent rises with each Store Expansion, and electricity with every rack, fridge and freezer.
More different products on the shelves bring more customers.
You are warned when your money will not cover the week's bills and wages.

Prices
Each rack shows today's market price for its product.
When you set a price, you hear how it stands: a normal price, below the market price, or too high.
Pricing on the Computer warns you about any price that is too high.

Marketing, festivals and daily tasks
The Marketing app on the Computer runs offers of 10, 20 or 30 percent on up to three products, and adverts: Leaflets, a Newspaper Ad, and from level 11 a Radio Ad.
A festival comes every 10 days, with Indian and world festivals. Expect a rush for the products it brings.
One daily task a day, with a reward of money, XP or a MarketHub coupon. The same kind of task never comes twice in five days.
Customer Reviews and Achievements open from Statistics.
Turn on Guided first day when you start a new game for step-by-step help through your first order, unloading, stocking and serving.

Sounds
New sounds for the UPI QR code, a customer calling for help, a payment going through, a customer joining a checkout line, a shoplifter being hit, and a fridge or freezer going in.
A cash sale plays each sound one after another, so you hear the drawer, the notes, the coins and the drawer closing.
Handing back a note in change now makes a sound, and so does every coin.
The closing sound plays the moment the store closes, by hand or at midnight.
You hear the mop when you or a cleaner start on a mess, and when it is done.

Fixes
An emptied delivery truck no longer stays at the dock and blocks the next one.
Saving tries again if the phone was busy, so no progress is lost.
TalkBack now says 1 item, 1 minute and 1 unpaid item, not 1 items.
What's New now comes after an update, one page at a time. The update message itself only says which version is ready.
